header.name: index
header.tagline: Map a workspace offline. Refute a claim the code does not support.

flows.title: How a structural claim is settled against the code itself
flows.alt: Eight stages from workspace discovery to a rechecked certificate. Fingerprints ask whether ground truth has moved, and a graph built over changed code is rebuilt before any claim is grounded against it. A claim is answered from the graph rather than from memory, ending as match, refuted or unverifiable.
flows.footnote: The verdict is computed from the graph, so an agent's confidence has no route into it.

stages.title: Discover
stages.note: The workspace is walked and pruned into a repo list.

stages.title: Classify
stages.note: Each repo takes its ecosystem from its own manifests.

stages.title: Graph
stages.note: Imports and symbols become edges carrying a file and line.

stages.title: Freshness
stages.note: Fingerprints answer one question: has ground truth moved?

stages.title: Claim
stages.note: An agent asserts a dependency, or that a symbol exists.

stages.title: Ground
stages.note: The claim meets the graph, and never the agent's memory.

stages.title: Certificate
stages.note: The verdict is sealed over a hash of the whole graph.

stages.title: Recheck
stages.note: A consumer recomputes that hash instead of trusting it.

returns.label: GROUND TRUTH MOVED: THE GRAPH IS REBUILT FIRST

outcomes.label: MATCH
outcomes.note: the graph carries the edge, with file and line

outcomes.label: REFUTED
outcomes.note: the graph is complete here, with no such edge

outcomes.label: UNVERIFIABLE
outcomes.note: an endpoint sits outside the scanned workspace
